claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53 with quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
An HPHT treatment of approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours is a suitable intervention for HfZrTiTa0.53.
Rapid quenching after HPHT will lock in the modified microstructure.
HPHT treatment will induce a hierarchically patterned microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The HPHT-treated alloy will contain refined grains.
The HPHT-treated alloy will contain coherent submicron precipitates at phase interfaces.
Grain refinement and coherent precipitates will promote dislocation mobility during dynamic loading.
The modified microstructure will promote twinning and multiple concurrent plasticity mechanisms during dynamic loading.
The coherent multiphase interface structure will distribute deformation more uniformly and increase strain hardening.
More uniformly distributed deformation will delay shear banding and strain localization.
Under adiabatic loading at strain rates of 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1, HPHT treatment will increase dynamic yield and compressive strengths by approximately 10–20% relative to the baseline.
Under the stated dynamic conditions, the treated alloy's fracture strain will exceed 13.5%.
The treated alloy will have greater resistance to dynamic strain localization than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit improved energy absorption under high-strain-rate loading.
The treated alloy will exhibit a moderated and more controlled impact-induced energy release.
Outside the strain-rate range of 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1, different deformation mechanisms may diminish the benefits of HPHT treatment.
Matched untreated and HPHT-treated HfZrTiTa0.53 specimens will be tested by adiabatic dynamic compression over 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1.

The hypothesis is falsified if the treated specimens lack the proposed microstructure or fail to achieve statistically significant improvements, including at least 10% gains in dynamic yield and compressive strengths plus enhanced uniform deformation.
